# RAGmen

> Turn any document corpus into a schema-grounded knowledge graph and a read-only retrieval layer. Ask questions, get cited answers.

RAGmen is an open source GraphRAG framework. It converts unstructured documents (PDF, Markdown, plain text) into a Neo4j knowledge graph using a schema approved by the user before any AI cost is spent, then serves cited answers over the Model Context Protocol (MCP).

## What RAGmen is

- A **three-component pipeline**: Blueprint (design) → Forge (build) → Serve + Agent (query)
- Every answer includes the **exact source document and page number**
- The AI is **strictly limited to your documents** — it refuses to answer from general knowledge
- When two documents **disagree**, both answers are shown with attribution
- Re-adding an **unchanged file costs nothing** — content-addressed deduplication
- **Interrupted runs resume** from the last completed chunk — never pay twice

## Components

- **forge** — build-time CLI: `forge add`, `forge cook`, `forge retract`, `forge conflicts`
- **lattice-serve** — read-only MCP server with hybrid retrieval (vector + keyword + graph, RRF fusion)
- **agent** — answer policy layer: enforced citations, conflict surfacing, corpus-only answers
- **blueprint** — design-time schema system with human approval gate before extraction

## Technology

- Python 3.11+
- Neo4j graph database (Docker)
- OpenAI (extraction) with prompt caching
- sentence-transformers (local embeddings)
- MCP (Model Context Protocol) for retrieval
- RapidFuzz for entity resolution

## Use cases

- Law firms querying contract archives
- Technical writers querying product manuals
- Policy teams querying regulatory documents
- Researchers querying scientific literature
- Anyone who needs cited, corpus-only answers from a body of documents

## Key differentiators from plain RAG

- **Closed schema**: the AI cannot invent entity types or relationships outside the approved blueprint
- **Graph traversal**: multi-hop questions that require following relationships across the document
- **Conflict detection**: explicit disagreement surfacing instead of silent last-write-wins
- **Provenance**: every edge in the graph carries the source chunk and character range
